clue.text: Leader of the windbags?

parts.note: the windbags are bagpipes, not talkers, and their leader heads a pipe band

explanation.surface: Someone is in charge of a crowd of long-winded bores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windbags' suggests people who talk too much; here it means the bags of bagpipes, so the leader is the head of a military pipe band.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior piper who directs a pipe band is given this rank title.

clue.text: Choose to express: gratitude to an old sycophant.

parts.note: to choose is to pick
to express gratitude is to thank

explanation.surface: Someone decides to say thank you to a fawning flatterer of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a flatterer who curries favour by toadying or telling tales.

clue.text: Interval for father to employ

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A break during which dad can be put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short break or interval in activity.

clue.text: Much slaughter 'in the, service area

parts.note: Mass is a church service
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: A bloodbath takes place where a service station stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a motorway service area; it is the church service, Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the indiscriminate killing of many people.

clue.text: Is it rigged up for trial purposes ?

definitions.text: Is it rigged up for trial purposes

parts.words: Is it rigged up for trial purposes
parts.note: a ship's makeshift spar is rigged up after damage, and 'trial' points to a court's panel of twelve

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a court case has been fixed in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigged' suggests fraud; at sea it means fitted with ropes. A jury mast is a temporary mast put up after the real one is lost, and juries sit at trials.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift replacement mast erected on a ship at sea after dismasting.

clue.text: She has a tiff with another girl

parts.note: a tiff is a quarrel, a row
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: One girl falls out with another.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowena is a woman's name, so it can stand for 'she'.

clue.text: His BA could make a gentleman of him

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be reworked into something new

parts.note: taken as written: the letters of his and BA

explanation.surface: Earning his degree might turn him into a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of HISBA, signalled by 'could make', gives SAHIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was a respectful Indian form of address for a European man, meaning sir or master.

clue.text: Fool of a woman

parts.note: she is a pronoun standing for a woman
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A dismissive phrase for a silly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a female donkey is a female fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A female donkey; an ass is also a byword for a fool.

clue.text: They succeed even in a man's world

definitions.text: They succeed even in a man's world

parts.words: They succeed even in a man's world
parts.note: succeed means come after as inheritors, not prosper, and these inheritors are female

explanation.surface: A remark about women who prosper in a male-dominated world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' looks like 'do well'; it means inherit, and the inheritors are women, even where estates usually pass to sons.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who are due to inherit property or titles.

clue.text: Outstandingly masterful?

parts.note: domineering, and also covered in raised knobs that stand out from a surface

explanation.surface: Someone is exceptionally commanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstandingly' seems to mean 'exceptionally'; it also means 'with parts standing out', since a boss is a raised stud or knob.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means domineering, and also studded with raised ornamental knobs.

clue.text: Just the one to run through a menu ?

definitions.text: Just the one to run through a menu ?

parts.words: Just the one to run through a menu
parts.note: a fast horse is built to run, and a meal is run through dish by dish, one course after another

explanation.surface: Someone is ideal for reading out a bill of fare.
explanation.walkthrough: A menu is made of courses, and this swift horse is literally a runner; one who runs through the courses.
explanation.definitionFit: A courser is a swift horse, a natural runner.

clue.text: We are up against calamities with these pests

parts.note: evils are misfortunes or calamities

explanation.surface: Someone laments being beset by disasters and vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: Weevils are beetles that damage grain and other crops.

clue.text: Letter shows the task is half completed

indicators.note: a job half completed has only its opening half done, so keep the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A note reports that the job is only halfway done.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Music by The Brothers in this garden ?

definitions.text: Music by The Brothers in this garden ?

parts.words: Music by The Brothers in this garden
parts.note: the brothers are monks, and Ketelbey's popular piece is set in a garden belonging to their house

explanation.surface: It reads like a concert billing for a band called The Brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Brothers' looks like a band; they are monks. 'In a Monastery Garden' is a well-known 1915 light orchestral piece by Albert Ketelbey.
explanation.definitionFit: A house where monks live together under religious vows.

clue.text: He makes a beeline for his work

definitions.text: He makes a beeline for his work

parts.words: He makes a beeline for his work
parts.note: making a beeline normally means heading straight somewhere; here the work itself is with bees

explanation.surface: A keen worker goes straight to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a beeline' means goes directly; read literally, his work is among bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper, someone who tends hives.

clue.text: Suggests a matter of duty to a clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone hints to a vicar that something is his duty.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means obligatory, as in 'it is incumbent on you'; as a noun it is the holder of a church living.

clue.text: The Thames, in part, is takin; one south

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A geography note: the river is heading south at one point.
explanation.walkthrough: IS takes on I and S. The Isis is the stretch of the Thames that flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is the name given to the upper reach of the river around Oxford.

clue.text: … Their products are good for : a season at least

definitions.text: Their products are good for : a season at least

parts.words: Their products are good for : a season at least
parts.note: season means flavour food, and the product dug from these workings is the commonest seasoning; also a byword for long hard labour

explanation.surface: Goods that last at least one season, such as clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a time of year; it is the verb 'flavour'. Salt from these workings seasons food, and being sent there means years of hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground workings where rock salt is dug out.

clue.text: Confections for, keeping 'washer-women's. hair in order?

definitions.text: Confections for, keeping 'washer-women's. hair in order?

parts.words: Confections for, keeping 'washer-women's. hair in order
parts.note: a buckets-and-tubs scene: a tub for washing and a knot of hair tied at the back of the head

explanation.surface: Something for laundry women to keep their hair tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer: a bath is what washer-women use, and buns keep hair in order. The sweet currant buns come from the city of Bath in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet, sugar-topped yeast buns originating in the English city of Bath.

clue.text: Rose for the meat

explanation.surface: A floral garnish for a meat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a class of climbing rose, and a small round boneless cut of lamb or other meat.

clue.text: Punters do this as well as place bets

definitions.text: Punters do this as well as place bets

parts.words: Punters do this as well as place bets
parts.note: punters seem to be gamblers, but in rugby a punt and a place-... are both ways to strike the ball with the foot

explanation.surface: Gamblers do this besides putting money on races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punters' and 'place bets' suggest betting; a punt and a place-kick are kinds of this action in football.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking a ball with the foot, which a punt and a place-kick both are.

clue.text: Pleasurable means 'of going around in the States

definitions.text: Pleasurable means 'of going around in the States

parts.words: Pleasurable means 'of going around in the States
parts.note: a fairground ride that turns in circles, under its American name

explanation.surface: An American way of getting about that is a pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means of going around' suggests transport; it is a fairground ride, called a merry-go-round in Britain and this in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for a merry-go-round, a revolving fairground ride.

clue.text: Proverbially a capital place for a tug-of-war

definitions.text: Proverbially a capital place for a tug-of-war

parts.words: Proverbially a capital place for a tug-of-war
parts.note: the proverb 'when Greek meets Greek, then comes the tug of war' points to the Greek capital

explanation.surface: A city is said to be excellent for a rope-pulling contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like 'excellent'; it is a capital city. The proverb says 'When Greek meets Greek, then comes the tug of war'.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Greece.

clue.text: How can' you make a cat sit still ?

indicators.note: asks how these letters can be made into something else, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet owner asks how to make the cat stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How can you make' signals an anagram of CATSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless, not moving.

clue.text: Painful outcome of running along the Border ?

definitions.text: Painful outcome of running along the Border ?

parts.words: Painful outcome of running along the Border
parts.note: running here is sewing a quick seam along a border of cloth, and a runner's side pain is also called a stitch

explanation.surface: A runner on a cross-border race gets a pain in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Border' suggests the Scottish border; it is the edge of fabric (the hem), and 'running' is a sewing stitch as well as jogging, which causes a stitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative needlework stitch used to finish the folded edge of cloth.

clue.text: .A flighty person might take to them

definitions.text: .A flighty person might take to them

parts.words: .A flighty person might take to them
parts.note: flighty here means inclined to flee, and to take to one's feet behind is to run away

explanation.surface: A fickle person might grow fond of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests fickle; it is used for someone given to flight, and 'take to one's heels' means run away.
explanation.definitionFit: The backs of the feet, which one takes to when fleeing.

clue.text: Churchill related its gather: ing

parts.note: the first volume of Churchill's war memoirs is titled 'The Gathering' followed by a word for a tempest

explanation.surface: A history note on Churchill recounting a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Gathering Storm' (1948) is the first volume of Winston Churchill's history of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent disturbance of the weather, with strong wind and rain.

clue.text: Some took a picture of an animal

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone photographed a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'of an animal' as the definition; 'of' is a link word, so the definition is just 'an animal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a giraffe-like African mammal of the Congo forests.

clue.text: Scene of large-scale operations

parts.note: operations seem military or surgical; they are big climbing expeditions on the world's highest peak

explanation.surface: A theatre of war or a big hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large-scale operations' suggests a war or surgery; it is mountaineering expeditions, and the scale is the mountain's height.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest mountain on Earth, site of huge climbing expeditions.

clue.text: At any rate it won't run people down

definitions.text: At any rate it won't run people down

parts.words: At any rate it won't run people down
parts.note: a railway service bound for London runs up, never down, at whatever speed; it also will not knock anyone over

explanation.surface: Something that, whatever happens, won't criticise anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run people down' looks like 'criticise'; trains towards London are 'up' trains, so this one carries people up, not down. 'At any rate' also hints at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A train travelling towards the main terminus, in British use usually London.

clue.text: What makes one fed up might be an asset

indicators.note: might be says the letters could become another word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that bores one might still be useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like 'bored'; it means well fed. 'Might be' signals an anagram of ASSET.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to satisfy fully, feeding someone until they want no more.

clue.text: They're prepared to be bought at their face value

definitions.text: They're prepared to be bought at their face value

parts.words: They're prepared to be bought at their face value
parts.note: face value means worth on the surface; here the value is to the face, as make-up is prepared preparations

explanation.surface: Things willing to be accepted for what they seem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face value' means apparent worth; literally, these preparations are valued for what they do to the face. 'Prepared' hints at preparations, a word for such products.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up and beauty preparations applied to the face.
